title: Unified invocation contracts and temporal join layer for Console analytics
creator: Evan Patel
description:
Background: Console telemetry currently flows through multiple ingestion pipelines (eventrouter, ingestion-worker, job-import) and ends up in siloed staging tables. Downstream analytics queries join on ad-hoc keys and suffer from duplication, inconsistent attribution, and slow temporal queries when joining streaming events with periodic snapshot tables. This work creates a canonical 'invocation contract' and a temporal-join layer that produces curated, query-optimized analytics tables for cost/latency attribution, SLA slicing, and feature adoption dashboards.

Goals:
- Define a single canonical invocation identifier and contract that all ingestion pipelines populate (invocation_id, started_at, finished_at, canonical_route, tenant_id, model_variant, invocation_phase).
- Implement a temporal-join materialization layer that reconciles streaming events, background batch snapshots, and late-arriving telemetry using event time semantics.
- Produce a set of curated marts: invocation_core_curated, invocation_latency_rollup, invocation_cost_segments, and invocation_debug_blob.
- Ensure incremental (delta) backfills are efficient and maintain provenance for audits.

Why this is different: Instead of denormalizing everything into huge session tables, the temporal-join approach keeps a compact canonical contract and derives multiple narrow marts suited to common Console queries, improving scan efficiency and simplifying long-term schema evolution.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical invocation_id is populated by all ingestion paths and validated against a schema (nulls allowed only for legacy imports)
A temporal-join materialized view exists that correctly associates start/end events with token-level telemetry within 99.9% accuracy on a 7-day sample

Curated tables (invocation_core_curated, invocation_latency_rollup, invocation_cost_segments) are populated hourly with <=30m latency for new data and provide partition pruning for queries by date and tenant_id
A documented rollback and replay procedure exists for reprocessing a 7-day window within 4 hours for a single shard
Dashboards for top-queries show >2x reduction in average scan bytes for the most common SLA and cost analyses after migration
implementation_notes: Schema: canonical columns: invocation_id (uuid), tenant_id, route_id, started_at (ts), finished_at (ts), status, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_microcents, kv_blob_ref
Partitioning: daily partition by date(started_at) with sub-partition by tenant_id hash for hot tenants

Temporal join strategy: use event_time watermarks and a 30m late-arrival buffer; implement as streaming delta merges into a compact canonical table, with event-type tagging to support idempotent merges
Storage: base tables in DeltaLake with Z-order on tenant_id, started_at to support typical query patterns; materialized rollups as BigQuery scheduled queries for BI consumers (if export required)
Provenance: add ingestion_source and ingestion_batch_id columns to support audit and replays
Backwards compatibility: support legacy imports by backfilling invocation_id via deterministic hashing of (tenant_id, route, started_at) with a flag set so downstream can treat as synthetic
migration_steps: 1) Schema design review with PM/design/infra — complete (doc linked below)
2) Update ingestion-worker to emit invocation_contract fields (staged in feature-flag) — PR opened
3) Deploy a non-authoritative canonical table in parallel (write-only from new pipelines) and run validator jobs against legacy joins for 2 weeks
4) Implement temporal-join materializer job (Spark Structured Streaming job) and run in 'dry-run' mode to validate outputs
5) Once validations pass, flip the feature-flag to make canonical invocation_id authoritative and backfill 30 days with delta pipeline
6) Create final curated marts and update dashboard queries and Looker views to point at new tables
7) Monitor query performance and costs for 2 weeks, then decommission legacy denormalized marts
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validators and merge logic (>=90% coverage)
Integration tests: end-to-end ingestion from eventrouter -> canonical table -> materializer -> curated_mart using a synthetic 7-day workload
Performance test: run common Console queries (SLA slice, tenant top-10 routes, cost-by-model) against both legacy and new marts and compare scan bytes and latency
Fault injection: simulate late arrivals (1hr, 6hr, 24hr) and verify reconciliation correctness and idempotence
Regression checks: nightly data diff job to detect divergence between legacy canonicalization and new contract for a rolling 14-day window
rollout_notes: Day 0: start dry-run materializer and run validators (no consumers switched)
Day 3: feature-flag small internal workspace to use canonical invocation_id (compare dashboards)
Day 7: opt-in beta for 5% of production workloads for curated marts (observability team to monitor)
Day 14: full cutover if metrics (accuracy, latency, cost) meet targets; otherwise iterate
Post-cutover: maintain legacy export for 30 days in read-only to enable emergency rollback

2025-02-03 QA: Dry-run materializer produced a 0.6% mismatch vs legacy on a 7-day sample; mismatches investigation points to out-of-order events in job-import pipeline. Plan: add sequence_number reconciliation and increase watermark to 45m for that source.
2025-02-07 Priya Raman: Adjusted temporal join watermark to 45m for job-import and added reconciliation job for seq gaps. Scheduling validation run for tomorrow.
Follow-ups: need a small design doc on synthetic invocation_id for legacy imports and a playbook for emergency rollbacks to legacy marts.
